subject.title: Feature/Fix: Add conservative lineage safety and promotion controls

question: Should CodexBar adopt this four-PR lineage accounting architecture, or continue with the narrower fork identity and cache invalidation approach in https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118?
rationale: Both paths target the same open overcount problem, but this PR introduces a large parallel accounting subsystem and promotion contract whose long-term maintenance direction cannot be decided by tests alone.

options.title: Prefer the narrow repair
options.body: Land the proven identity and cache invalidation fix first, then require evidence that a separate lineage authority subsystem remains necessary.

options.title: Sponsor the lineage stack
options.body: Approve the four-PR architecture and require exact-head real-corpus and upgrade proof before each stacked landing step.

options.title: Pause both approaches
options.body: Keep the investigation open while defining the permanent scanner accounting contract and shared acceptance corpus.

recommendation.title: Prefer the narrow repair
recommendation.body: Land the proven identity and cache invalidation fix first, then require evidence that a separate lineage authority subsystem remains necessary.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a repository-level architecture and maintenance tradeoff rather than a mechanical code repair.
